title: feat(brains): an output token bound on the ask contract
description:
## .what

the brain ask contract (context.brain.choice.ask, BrainAtom.ask) accepts no bound on output tokens, so a caller cannot cap a single generation. the provider own limit is the only cap.

checkable evidence: rhachet@1.48.1 exposes no max-output or max-thought option on ask, and rhachet-brains-openrouter@0.1.3 sends no max_tokens in its request body. in ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhrain, four review asks on openrouter/deepseek/flash ended with finish_reason=length at 131,072 output tokens and contentLength 0 (for example generation gen-1791007661-ezKsM4RJYqxHj1TVGfg8). a review verdict is a json object of a few thousand tokens; no honest reply is near 131k.

## .why

a runaway is billed in full and returns no verdict, so the caller pays for a malfunction and then pays again for the re-run. a caller that knows its reply size has no way to make the runaway fail early and cheap.

## .shape of the fix

- add an optional output bound to the ask input, for example { limit: { output: { tokens: 32000 } } } (name it to match the contract vocabulary; distinct from the effort / reasoning budget in #595 and #490, which bound the think, not the whole reply)
- each brain adapter forwards it to its provider (max_tokens on openrouter and openai-shaped apis); an adapter that cannot honor it says so rather than drops it in silence
- a reply cut at the bound surfaces as the extant output-limit error, with the realized spend at the bound
- clamp: a stubbed adapter asserts the bound reaches the request body; an absent bound sends naught (behavior unchanged)

the openrouter half is filed on ehmpathy/rhachet-brains-openrouter.
